newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields rise, crown softens to dollar.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields rise, crown softens to dollar.

text.p: Swedish bond yields ended higher on Friday, lifted by U.S. statistics, and the crown firmed against the mark but softened against the dollar, breaking through the important eight crown level.
Bond yields were first hurt by climbing European yields and then by higher than expected U.S. non-farm payrolls and NAPM figures. But Sweden did not belong to the largest losers.
"We are holding on fairly well against Germany," said one trader who was not too worried about the rise.
"Now we'll have to see what happens abroad. Sweden isn't trading on it's own merits," he said.
The 10-year bond yield rose nine basis points to 6.47 percent and the six-month T-bill advanced two basis points to 4.30 percent.
The crown weakened to 8.0270 against the dollar from 7.9684 late on Thursday while it firmed to 4.3260 against the mark from 4.3335.

"The weakening of the crown against the dollar is entirely dollar driven. We haven't seen any large customer flows. It's only been pure interbank trading. It feels like you should keep dollars," one dealer said.
